$comment: What the AiSOC SDKs promise, per language, and every place one of them does not deliver it.
Enforced by scripts/check_sdk_surface.py, which reads this in both directions: a language with
no recorded gap must actually reach the namespace, and a recorded gap must still be a gap. So
this list only shrinks -- filling a gap without deleting its entry here fails the build.
The three sdk-* CI jobs cannot see any of this. They compile and run each package in isolation,
which is how packages/sdk-go came to hold three green ticks over a file of type declarations.

go.gap: packages/sdk-go ships go.mod and aisoc/models.go, and that file is type and const declarations only -- no functions, no net/http. There is no Go client to check against the spec, so every namespace below is a gap in Go rather than an implementation. Recorded here rather than exempted quietly, because sdk-go-test builds, vets and tests it green and a reader takes that tick for parity. The gate re-derives this: the day a file in the package imports net/http, this entry is stale and the build fails until it is replaced by the namespaces the client reaches.

gaps.python: The responder namespaces (approvals, push, oncall, live-actions) were added to the TypeScript client for the PWA and the native app and have no Python equivalent yet. The routes are in docs/openapi.yaml already, which is why nobody noticed: the spec is complete and the ergonomic surface is not.
Web Push subscription management is browser-shaped -- a Python caller has no service worker to register -- so the asymmetry is deliberate rather than an oversight.
Reachable from the TypeScript responder client only; no Python caller has asked for the rota yet.

Discovery and dry-run are exposed in TypeScript for the responder surfaces. Dispatch is deliberately absent from both clients: a live containment goes through the approval path so an approver is bound to it, and the API exposes no un-approved dispatch route to proxy.
